rules.title: A catch-all discard says why the failure cannot matter
rules.text: `except:` and `except Exception:` take every failure the block can raise, including the programming mistakes nobody wrote a handler for, and a body that discards the failure leaves the caller reading an ordinary result: the exceptions the block can answer for are named, or the line says why the failure cannot matter.

judgement.question: Does this catch-all discard the failure without saying why the failure cannot matter?

criteria.true: the handler takes every application failure and discards it, and nothing beside the handler says why the failure cannot matter
criteria.false: the handler records the failure, raises it or a replacement the caller handles, re-runs the work, or the handler (or a comment beside it) says why the failure cannot matter
